He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]] and [[high school basketball]] for [[Needham Broughton High School]]. ==High school career== Graham attended [[Needham B. Broughton High School|Broughton High School]] in [[Raleigh, North Carolina]]. As a senior, Graham averaged 15.7 points and 5.4 assists per game, leading the team to a 26–6 record and the 4A state championship game during the 2012–13 season.{{Cite web|date=2014-07-21|title=Devonte' Graham|url=https://kuathletics.com/roster/devonte-graham/|access-date=2021-04-14|website=Kansas Jayhawks|language=en-US|archive-date=April 14, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210414150423/https://kuathletics.com/roster/devonte-graham/|url-status=dead}} Graham originally committed to [[Appalachian State Mountaineers men's basketball|Appalachian State]] before deciding he wanted to play elsewhere. However, Appalachian State's head coach at the time, [[Jason Capel]], would not allow him to de-commit, as he felt other teams may have been tampering with Graham following his commitment to the university. Due to this, Graham elected to play a [[post-graduate year]] at [[Brewster Academy]], in [[Wolfeboro, New Hampshire]], rather than honor his commitment to play for Appalachian State.{{cite news|last1=Newell|first1=Jesse|title=Appalachian State coach who let Devonte' Graham go says he has regrets|url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/spt-columns-blogs/campus-corner/article77253202.html|access-date=June 14, 2017|date=May 12, 2016}} At Brewster Academy, Graham averaged 17.2 points and 5.0 assists per game, leading the team to the national prep championship and the New England championship during the 2013–14 season. On May 2, 2014, Graham committed to [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], choosing them over [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|North Carolina State]] and [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]].{{cite web|title=Devonte Graham|url=http://www.kuathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=5848|website=[[Kansas Jayhawks]]|access-date=June 14, 2017}} ==College career== [[File:Devonte' Graham 2016.jpg|thumb|150px|left|Graham with the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]] in 2016]] As a freshman at Kansas, Graham averaged 5.7 points and 2.1 assists per game. He had a season-high 20 points against [[Texas Christian University|TCU]] on February 21, 2015. In the NCAA Tournament, he scored 17 points against [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State]]. After scoring a then career-high 27 points on 8-of-13 shooting against [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma]], Graham was named Big 12 Player of the Week for the week of February 14, 2016.{{cite web |url=http://www.big12sports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_LANG=C&ATCLID=210715493&DB_OEM_ID=10410 |title=Wins Over Ranked Foes Help Graham, Burton To Weekly Honors |publisher=Big 12 Sports |date=February 15, 2016 |access-date=February 15, 2016}} At the conclusion of the regular season, Graham was named to the Big 12 All-Defensive Team.{{cite web|title=Nation's Best Lead All-Big 12 Men's Basketball Awards |url=http://www.big12sports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_LANG=C&ATCLID=210776703&DB_OEM_ID=10410 |website=Big 12 Sports |access-date=March 6, 2016 |date=March 6, 2016}} He was named MVP of the [[2016 Big 12 men's basketball tournament]] after scoring 27 points against [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia]] in the championship game.{{cite news|title=No. 1 Kansas overcomes No. 9 West Virginia to capture Big 12 title|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400871094|access-date=June 14, 2017|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=March 12, 2016}} As a sophomore in the 2015–16 season, Graham averaged 11.3 points per game while shooting 46 percent overall and 44 percent from 3 point territory.{{cite news|last1=Bedore|first1=Gary|title=Devonté Graham's personality and play pleases Self, youngsters alike|url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article102762252.html|access-date=June 14, 2017|work=[[Kansas City Star]]|date=September 19, 2016}}Trotter, Jake. [https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/22918865/kansas-jayhawks-devonte-graham-led-team-final-four In big moments, Devonte' Graham has been Kansas' X factor all season], ESPN, March 26, 2018. As a junior, Graham was named to the Second Team All-Big 12.{{cite web|title=Three Teams Lead Men's Basketball Awards |url=http://www.big12sports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=106110&SPID=13134&DB_OEM_ID=10410&ATCLID=211514295 |website=Big 12 Sports |access-date=March 11, 2017 |date=March 5, 2017}} Along with [[Frank Mason III]], Graham formed the backcourt of a Kansas team that went 31–5 but lost in the Elite Eight, as Graham shot 0 for 7 from the field and missed six 3-pointers in a season-ending 74–60 loss to [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]]. For the season, he averaged 13.4 points, 4.1 assists and 3.1 rebounds per game. In April, Graham announced on Twitter that he was returning for his senior year.{{cite news|last1=Galloway|first1=Matt|title=KU basketball guard Devonte' Graham returning for senior season|url=http://cjonline.com/sports/hawkzone/2017-04-09/ku-basketball-guard-devonte-graham-returning-senior-season|access-date=June 14, 2017|work=[[Topeka Capital-Journal]]|date=April 9, 2017}} In his senior season, Graham was named the preseason Big 12 Player of the Year for the 2017–18 season.{{cite news|last1=Tait|first1=Matt|title=KU's Devonté Graham named Big 12 preseason player of the year|url=http://www2.kusports.com/news/2017/oct/12/kus-devonte-graham-named-big-12-preseason-player-y/?mens_basketball|access-date=October 13, 2017|work=kusports.com|date=October 13, 2017}} On November 28, Graham scored a career high 35 points in a 96–58 win over [[University of Toledo|Toledo]].{{cite web |url=http://kusports.com/news/2017/nov/28/devonte-graham-and-no-2-jayhawks-too-hot-toledo/?mens_basketball=&templates |title=Devonte' Graham and No. 2 Jayhawks too hot for Toledo |work=KUSports.com |date= November 28, 2017 |access-date= November 28, 2017 |last=Smith |first=Benton}} The following game, a 76–60 win over [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]], Graham again scored 35 points.{{cite news|title=Graham's 35 carries No. 2 Kansas past Syracuse, 76–60|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400986115|access-date=January 15, 2018|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}} Graham would go on to be unanimously selected as the Big 12 Player of the Year, averaging 17.6 points and 7.2 assists per game as a senior.{{cite news|last1=Trotter|first1=Jake|title=Devonte' Graham unanimous Big 12 Player of the Year over Trae Young|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/22644618/kansas-jayhawks-devonte-graham-unanimous-big-12-player-year-oklahoma-sooners-trae-young|work=[[ESPN.com]]|access-date=March 13, 2018|date=March 13, 2018}} He was also named a consensus member of the First Team All-America by multiple organizations, leading his team to the 2017-18 Final Four in San Antonio, Texas. During his senior season, he averaged about 38 minutes a game. ==Professional career== ===Charlotte Hornets / Greensboro Swarm (2018–2021)=== Graham was drafted in the 2nd round, 34th overall, of the [[2018 NBA draft]] by the [[Atlanta Hawks]] before being traded to the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in exchange for two second round picks.{{cite news |last1=Marks |first1=Brenda |title=Hornets trade up in NBA draft, select NC native in Kansas' Devonte' Graham |url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/nba/charlotte-hornets/article213635149.html |access-date=October 8, 2018 |work=[[The Charlotte Observer]] |date=June 22, 2018}} In the Hornets' first three summer league games, he averaged ten points and six assists per contest. However, he would miss the rest of summer league with a knee injury.{{cite news |last1=Bonnell |first1=Rick |title=There's good news regarding Charlotte Hornets rookie Devonte Graham's knee injury |url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/nba/charlotte-hornets/article215504635.html |access-date=October 8, 2018 |work=The Charlotte Observer |date=July 25, 2018}} Graham made his NBA debut on October 22, 2018, against the [[Toronto Raptors]], recording no points and one assist in five and a half minutes of play.{{cite web|url=http://www2.ljworld.com/weblogs/hawks_nba/2018/oct/31/devonte-graham-is-headed-to-the-g-league/|title=Devonte' Graham is headed to the G League|first=Benton|last=Smith|work='Hawks in the NBA|publisher=[[Lawrence Journal-World]]|date=October 31, 2018|access-date=December 5, 2018}} On October 23, 2019, Graham scored 23 points along with eight assists and four rebounds in a 126–125 win over the [[Chicago Bulls]]. Graham hit six three-pointers to help the Hornets set a new franchise record for three-point field goals made in a single game.{{cite web|title=Hornets rookie Washington nets 27 in 126–125 win over Bulls|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160625|date=October 23, 2019|website=ESPN.com|access-date=October 23, 2019}} On December 11, 2019, Graham scored a career-high 40 points with five rebounds and five assists in a 113–108 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web|title=Graham scores 1, Hornets rally to beat Nets 113–108|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401161002|date=December 11, 2019|website=ESPN.com|access-date=December 11, 2019}} In the 2019-2020 NBA season Graham had his best season averaging 18.2 points per game, and 7.5 assists per game (8th most in the NBA) and finished 5th in the league’s most improved player voting. Graham was featured on [[The Dodo (website)|The Dodo]]'s [[YouTube]] channel in June 2021, in a video about his basketball career and his life with his German Shepherd dog 'Charlotte', who is named after the Hornets.{{Citation|title=NBA Player's German Shepherd Is The Biggest Daddy's Girl {{!}} The Dodo Teammates| date=June 28, 2021 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=B5olmqctKy4|language=en|access-date=2021-08-21}}{{Cite web|date=2021-06-28|title=Devonte Graham and his dog spread love on social media|url=https://www.ksnt.com/sports/kansas-jayhawks/devonte-graham-and-his-dog-spread-love-on-social-media/|access-date=2021-08-21|website=KSNT News|language=en-US}} ===New Orleans Pelicans (2021–2023)=== On August 7, 2021, Graham was traded to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] in a three-team trade involving the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-acquire-jonas-valanciunas-devonte-graham-three-team-trade-memphis-grizzlies-charlotte-hornets|title=Pelicans acquire Valančiūnas and Graham in three-team trade with Grizzlies and Hornets|work=NBA.com|date=August 7, 2021}} He made his Pelicans debut on October 20, recording 18 points and five assists in a 117–97 loss to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{Cite web |title=JOEL EMBIID, FURKAN KORKMAZ HELP 76ERS BEAT PELICANS 117-97 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100009 |access-date=February 21, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On November 26, Graham hit a game-winning three-pointer with 1.9 seconds left to give the Pelicans a 98–97 win over the [[Utah Jazz]].{{Cite web |title=GRAHAM'S 3-POINTER LIFTS PELICANS TO 98-97 WIN OVER JAZZ |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100289 |access-date=February 21, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On December 15, he hit a 61-foot, buzzer-beating shot to hoist the Pelicans to a 113–110 win over the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]]. The shot set the NBA record for the longest buzzer-beating game-winner in league history, beating out [[Mahmoud Abdul-Rauf]]'s 55-foot shot in 1992 for the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{Cite web|title=Watch: Devonte' Graham beats Thunder with NBA record buzzer-beater|url=https://fansided.com/2021/12/15/devonte-graham-pelicans-buzzer-beater-nba-record-video/|url-status=live|access-date=December 15, 2021|website=Fansided|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211216042950/https://fansided.com/2021/12/15/devonte-graham-pelicans-buzzer-beater-nba-record-video/ |archive-date=December 16, 2021 |archive-date=December 16, 2021 }} On March 24, 2022, Graham scored a season-high 30 points, alongside two rebounds and four assists, in a 126–109 win over the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{Cite web |title=GRAHAM, MCCOLLUM LEAD PELICANS PAST BULLS 126-109 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022101098 |access-date=February 21, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} After a set of [[NBA Play-In Tournament|play-in tournament]] wins, the Pelicans qualified for the playoffs for the first time since [[2018 NBA playoffs|2018]] and faced the [[Phoenix Suns]] during their first-round series. Graham made his playoff debut on April 17, playing ten minutes in a 110–99 Game 1 loss.{{Cite web |title="CLASSIC CHRIS" STELLAR DOWN STRETCH, SUNS BEAT PELS 110-99 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042100141 |access-date=February 21, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} ===San Antonio Spurs (2023–2024)=== On February 9, 2023, Graham was traded, alongside four second-round picks, to the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in exchange for [[Josh Richardson]].{{cite web|title=Pelicans acquire Josh Richardson|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-acquire-josh-richardson-trade-spurs-devonte-graham|website=NBA.com|access-date=February 9, 2023}} Graham made his Spurs debut a day later, recording a season-high 31 points, three rebounds and three assists in a 138–131 double overtime loss to the [[Detroit Pistons]]. Graham's 31 points were also the most points scored in a debut in Spurs history.{{cite web|title=Bogandovic's 32 lead Pistons to double OT win over Spurs|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401468990|website=ESPN.com|access-date=February 10, 2023}}{{cite web|first=Angelo|last=Guinhawa|title=Tim Duncan who? Devonte' Graham sets wild record never seen in Spurs history|url=https://clutchpoints.com/spurs-news-tim-duncan-who-devonte-graham-sets-wild-record-never-seen-in-san-antonio-history|website=ClutchPoints.com|date=February 10, 2023|access-date=February 10, 2023}} On August 2, 2023, Graham was suspended for two games without pay for pleading guilty to a DWI charge.{{cite web|title=NBA suspends Spurs' Devonte' Graham for two games without pay|url=https://www.nba.com/news/nba-suspends-spurs-devonte-graham|website=NBA.com|date=August 2, 2023|access-date=August 2, 2023}} On April 12, 2024, Graham put up a game-winner in a 121–120 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web|first=Jedd|last=Pagaduan|title=Victor Wembanyama, Devonte Graham's heroics in Spurs' win vs. Nuggets spark proud Gregg Popovich reaction|url=https://clutchpoints.com/spurs-news-victor-wembanyama-devonte-grahams-heroics-vs-nuggets-spark-proud-gregg-popovich-reaction|website=ClutchPoints.com|date=April 12, 2024|access-date=April 12, 2024}} On July 6, 2024, Graham was traded back to the [[Charlotte Hornets]] alongside a future second-round pick in exchange for cap space, but was waived immediately.{{cite web|title=Charlotte Hornets Acquire Second-Round Pick And Devonte' Graham From San Antonio 31, he signed with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]],{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Sign Devonte' Graham|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-sign-devonte-graham|website=NBA.com|date=July
